(performance, small; console-era remnant): lights are loaded per object draw in the console's eight-register model, with each world light moved into v
note: 11-18 (the harness's Map report, checked at 241395b49): one point light lights the scene: of those asking since the last choice the nearest takes slot 4, the rest are dropped (LightPointCtrl::requestPointLightBy, LightPointCtrl.cpp:54-65), its falloff the GX STEEP curve with a brightness clamped to 0.95..0.999999 (:60-62). 5.H.3: a mod's light competes for the one slot. Modern form: every requested light lit from the step's list; where two disc actors ask at once the picture differs from today's nearest-only (no step reads it). 11-18 (the harness's Mii report, checked at 241395b49): the Mii icon's light is moved into view space on the CPU and set into light slot 0 (MiiFaceTexture.cpp:272-279). 11-18 (the harness's native/src report, checked at 241395b49): a model channel's light mask is a u8 with its diffuse and attenuation as function codes (NebulaModelChannel, nebula_model.h:197-198), so at most eight lights reach a material. 11-18 (the harness's runtime/src/render/materials report, checked at 241395b49): the lit programs read at most 24 lights because the masks ride in float constants (fur.hlsl:38-39, mii_face.hlsl:33, normal_map.hlsl:48): a light past the 24th lights nothing without a word. 11-18 (the harness's runtime/src/render/programs report, checked at 241395b49): the cooked pixel programs light a channel as the console does: material colour times saturate((ambient * 255 + light_term(set, 2u, 3u, 2u, eye, N)) / 255), the lights picked by slot from the draw's set with the diffuse and attenuation codes (p004fd6cc:22-29; channel_lines and light_list, programs.rs:1042-1055), the eye position and a nointerpolation set index from the vertex program (v00fa2c22:15-17, :29-32).

title: (performance, small; same family as P-139): every visible actor scans every light area every step to find which one it stands in.
note: 11-18 (the harness's AreaObj report, checked at 241395b49): every area kind is found the same way: AreaObjMgr::find_in tests each area of the kind, last first (AreaObj.cpp:119-129), and MR::getAreaObj(name, pos) finds the manager by hashing the name a prefix at a time on every query (AreaObjContainer.cpp:405-431).

title: (console-era remnant, handling in the game's code): NormalMapBase remakes its normal maps on the CPU (swapColorGB, NormalMapBase.cpp:525 on: each RGBA8 texel's normal decoded and written as 0, g, b, r) and builds an LA8 lighting gradient on the CPU (createGradTexture, :483-523), with draw settings of its own (drawMaterialSetting, setStageForObject).
note: Found by the inventory under file 08 section 3's test (11-18). Modern form: the cooked normal map used as it is, lit in the shader by the renderer's lighting; nothing remade on the CPU. The shader side read 11-18 (CONSOLE-FREE.md section 3): normal_map.hlsl restates the console's stages (per-vertex light channels in 0-255 units, the indirect stage's 8-bit normal, four clamped stages, the last doubled); the draw finds its materials by name each time; the CPU ramp's scramble (rows 0-3) is never sampled. Proof: the gate's pictures of the levels with normal-mapped objects, the replay identical. 11-18 (the harness's MapObj report, checked at 241395b49): also the disc's .nrm.txt parsed as text at every actor's setup (NormalMapBase.cpp:81-85, loadData :555-566).
